This is essentially the same approach we took last year, except now Origination and Trading are separated. Regarding Assistants – we need to set their bonus targets directly rather than having OOC make those decisions. For non-commercial roles, as we discussed earlier this week, we also need to provide their targets.

Our main challenge remains how to leverage the GCS system and avoid the manual back-and-forth between Excel and GCS that we experienced last year. We are collaborating with Jennifer Stanton and the GCS team on this issue.

VPs will need to go through the final Corporate-wide PRC, adding another step for them. The outcomes from the ENA meeting should align with how all employees are rated going into the final meeting (e.g., 10/80/10 distribution, 1-100 scale).

Best,  
Michelle

-----Original Message-----  
From: Brennan, John  
Sent: Tuesday, October 16, 2001 1:17 PM  
To: Taylor, Laura  
Subject:

Here’s our PRC plan:

Assistants:  
Supervisors will rank 1, 2, 3 – compensation determined by Laura and me. No meetings required.

Non-Commercial (North America):  
Traditional ranking with appropriate attendees at meetings. Pay grid set by OOC.

Analysts and Associates:  
Rankings based on Billy Lemmons’ percentages; pay grid set by OOC. I prefer a 25% - 65% - 10% distribution, though Billy disagrees. This simplifies meetings by avoiding splitting into four groups and excluding top performers.

Managers/Directors:  
Rank 1 to 100 across clusters as deemed appropriate. Managers and directors combined in one table. Rankings tied directly to pay. Two meetings planned – one for traders, one for other commercial staff (origination, finance, etc.). No separate pay PRC; results will guide compensation discussions with leaders post-meetings. Promotions will also be decided at this time using separate criteria.

VPs:  
All VPs will be ranked 1 to 100 by a selected panel including some VPs and MDs. Ranking will directly influence pay.

Cheers, as you Brits say.
</body>
